pairs.subject: quality-gates
pairs.evidence: src/lib/org/security.ts:150 The register re-implements a two-condition subset of the gate instead of asking the shared resolver, while the real ?security=1 endpoint also applies the org bar or archetype default and the admission overlay, so a repo shown as passing can get a 422 from the snippet this same module generates.

techniques.evidence: src/lib/org/security.ts:150 Surfaces understate what blocks: policyFromParams spreads defaultGatePolicy(archetype) under the params and resolveRepoGatePolicy tightens further, but security.ts uses neither. The display-cap half is done correctly (lines 209-212 and buildGateSnippet read the full register).
src/lib/org/security.ts:165 A repo with no D9 row fails closed and the reason says 'D9 not measured' instead of printing a substitute score.
src/lib/security/supply-chain.ts:2 The externally moving Dependabot feed is kept out of the score the gate reads, so an overnight advisory cannot refuse an unchanged commit.
src/lib/org/security.ts:263 The exit path holds: curl -f turns the gate's 422 or 503 into a non-zero exit in the adopter's CI.

pairs.subject: quality-gates
pairs.evidence: src/app/api/org/scan/route.ts:89 The refusals seen in these routes are authorization, watch scope and credit entitlement, not quality checks on a change; a case-insensitive search of src/app/api/org, src/app/api/cron and src/lib/db for pre-push, waiver, exit code, merge gate and quality gate found zero files.

pairs.subject: quality-gates
pairs.evidence: src/lib/standard/doctor.ts:193 The doctor's only hard guardrail runs only if the gated repo's own manifest declares the pointer, so deleting paths.guardrails turns a would-be fail into no finding at all, not even the 'unchecked' this runner emits when git is missing.

techniques.evidence: src/lib/standard/doctor.ts:193 The gated party writes the input that enables the check, and not writing it is silent, although the spec says guardrails always ship.

src/lib/standard/doctor.ts:257 wired() searches raw hook text with comments included and across all stages, so '# lint' or a pre-commit entry reads as a wired pre-push control. standard.test.ts pins word boundaries only, with no comment-stripping or seeded prose case.

src/lib/standard/doctor.ts:202 Bare names like .env and id_rsa are root-only pathspecs (git ls-files -- route.ts returns 0 here against 180 nested route.ts), so a nested .env passes while the message claims the property holds rather than 'no listed path'.

src/lib/standard/doctor.ts:304 A named generatedFrom file that is absent skips freshness with no finding, though the zero-weight 'unchecked' level exists and the spec requires a skipped clause to be emitted. Git-unavailable cases are handled correctly.

src/lib/standard/wiring.ts:26 The generated workflow claims a merge block, but nothing under src/lib/standard or src/lib/onboarding tells the adopter to make the conformance job a required check, so red only reaches the run log.

src/lib/standard/wiring.ts:54 The job runs doctor --json with no continue-on-error and the doctor exits 1 on any fail, so the label is false. Separately, spec.ts:194 calls missing pre-push controls highest-severity while doctor.ts:265 emits them as warn, which never moves the exit code.
src/lib/standard/wiring.ts:1 The same in-repo script runs pre-push and in CI, so the remote run confirms the local one.
src/lib/standard/wiring.ts:5 The control extends the repo's existing hook system instead of installing a second one.
src/lib/standard/doctor.ts:215 A zero population is a failure rather than a clean pass, and could-not-judge has its own 'unchecked' level; the CI checkout is the backstop for the announced git skip.
src/lib/standard/doctor.ts:151 Findings carry a fix line, and this out-of-tree remedy degrades to an action that needs no Ascent install.
src/lib/standard/doctor.ts:520 A network failure during report-back is logged and never reaches the exit code, which keys on tree-derived fails only.
src/lib/standard/guardrails.ts:22 The blocking pattern list deliberately excludes near-miss globs that would match legitimate files.
